para.en: We might not think of ourselves as global citizens yet, but it’s both necessary and possible to do so. Some people are skeptical about the idea of global citizenship, but for most of human history, people didn’t think of themselves as citizens of nation-states. After all, for most of human history, nation-states didn’t exist. The rise of nation-states over the last few centuries has led people to add state citizenship to other identities, such as family, people group, or religion. Given the connections between people around the world and the common challenges we face, we need to layer global citizenship on to these other identities. This doesn’t mean that global citizenship replaces these other identities. There’s not a single story about our identities. Instead, it’s precisely because we have obligations to our families, those in our community, and those around the world.

Among unsatisfied professionals, there’s a repeating theme — the belief that someday (a mysterious day in the future) things will miraculously change and they’ll stumble into the perfect job or career. At the same time, they (typically) do little to meaningfully alter their current situation. They don’t like their job, so what do they do? They head to job boards and search for roles with a similar job title, hoping that the universe will sprinkle a bit of magic on their career if they just hit the refresh button in a different department or company. Efforts like this make professionals feel like they are doing something, when really they’re just setting themselves up to take a new role and quickly become just as disenchanted as they were before. It’s like rearranging deck chairs on the Titanic. You’ve got to completely switch up your approach. If you keep playing the same game, you’ll win the same prizes.

Sociologists argue that our perception and usage of time are not just basic properties of nature, like a clock ticking away in the background, nor are they simply psychological phenomena of individual experience. Instead, how we perceive and understand time is to a large degree shaped by tradition and cultural norms. Eviatar Zerubavel’s work, The Seven Day Circle: The History and Meaning of the Week, demonstrates how the week, a fundamental unit of time, is a social invention that varies across cultures, influencing how people structure their activities and rhythms of life. Why do we consider a nine-to-five job routine? Why don’t many of us work on the weekends? Why do we usually pay our bills at the end of the month? Why is the retirement age sixty-five? These numbers and patterns aren’t really dictated by nature or any essential human characteristic, but are rather social creations that we internalize and come to accept as “normal.”

In recent years, the number of illegal actions in particular at the corporate level has grown, or at least the number of cases that came to light, increased. Such misconduct has often only been exposed because brave informants have risked a great deal in order to put an end to it. Hence, it is no surprise that whistleblower protection has come into focus. If violations of law and order go undetected and unpunished for years because employees of a company fear to report illegal activities for fear of reprisals or consequences, it can have several negative effects. It can harm the company itself, but also third-parties, the economy in general, the general public, and even the rule of law could be affected. Protecting those who would assist in reducing unlawful or even criminal behaviour has two main functions: Protecting the individual’s actions as well as protecting the public good. A well-balanced whistleblower protection may have positive effects on both of these.

Unfortunately, sometimes the idea of a goal is disconnected from the daily reality of what it will take to achieve it. We fall in love with the idea of a goal, pushing out of mind how different our day-to-day will need to be for us to make it happen. In fact, research even suggests that positive fantasies about our future can lead us to put less effort into our goals because our fantasies provide us with a false and premature sense of accomplishment. We romanticize a goal — falling in love with the idea of a change. In the process, we gloss over the intricacies and challenges of integrating a complex new behavior into our life. As one study nicely summed it up, fantasizing about a positive future “seduces a person to mentally enjoy the desired future in the here and now” — and because we don’t reflect on why our fantasy is not yet our future, “a necessity to act is not induced.”

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) took on — (B) dismiss — (C) coexist with
(A) took on — (B) cultivate — (C) push aside
(A) gave up — (B) dismiss — (C) push aside
(A) took on — (B) cultivate — (C) coexist with
(A) gave up — (B) cultivate — (C) coexist with
choice.ex: ④ (A) took on (B) cultivate (C) coexist with 근거 ❷❹❺❻ 해설: (A) ❷ 과거엔 국민 국가의 시민이라 여기지 않았지만 ❹ 국민 국가의 부상이 국가 시민 정체성을 더하게 함 = 받아들였다(took on) / (B) ❺ 연결과 공통 과제를 고려할 때 세계 시민 정체성을 쌓을 필요 = 기르다(cultivate) / (C) ❻ 다른 정체성들을 대체하지 않음 = 공존하다(coexist with). gave up(버렸다)은 ❹의 ‘더하다(add)’와 반대, dismiss(일축하다)는 ❺의 필요성 주장과 반대, push aside(밀어내다)는 ❻ replaces와 같은 뜻이라 뒤의 not to replace them 과 모순. 요약문 해석: 사람들은 역사 대부분의 기간 동안 자신을 국민 국가의 구성원으로 보지 않았지만, 그 국가들이 생겨나자 그러한 정체성을 (A) 받아들였다. 마찬가 지로, 오늘날 세계의 유대와 공유된 문제들은 우리에게 세계적 정체성을 (B) 기를 것을 요구하는데, 그것은 우리가 이미 지닌 정체성들을 대체하는 것이 아니라 그것들과 (C) 공존하기 위한 것이다.
choice.psg: ❶ We might not think of ourselves as global citizens yet, but it’s both necessary and possible to do so. ❷ Some people are skeptical about the idea of global citizenship, but for most of human history, people didn’t think of themselves as citizens of nation-states. ❸ After all, for most of human history, nation-states didn’t exist. ❹ The rise of nation-states over the last few centuries has led people to add state citizenship to other identities, such as family, people group, or religion. ❺ Given the connections between people around the world and the common challenges we face, we need to layer global citizenship on to these other identities. ❻ This doesn’t mean that global citizenship replaces these other identities. ❼ There’s not a single story about our identities. ❽ Instead, it’s precisely because we have obligations to our families, those in our community, and those around the world.
choice.body: Although people did not see themselves as members of nation-states for most of history, they (A)________ such an identity once those states arose. Likewise, the ties and shared problems of today’s world call on us to (B)________ a global identity, which is meant to (C)________ the identities we already hold, not to replace them.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

choice.ex: ⑤ (A) far-fetched (B) recent (C) multifaceted 근거 ❷❸❹❼❽ 해설: (A) ❷ 세계 시민 개념에 회의적(skeptical) = 비현실적인(far-fetched) / (B) ❸ 역사 대부분 동안 국민 국가는 없었고 ❹ 지난 몇 세기 동안 부상 = 최근 의(recent) / (C) ❼ 정체성에 관한 이야기는 하나가 아님 + ❽ 가족·공동체·세계에 대한 의무 = 다면적인(multifaceted). appealing(매력적인)은 회의론자의 시각과 반대이고 역접 but과도 맞지 않음, ancient(고대의)는 ❸❹와 반대, uniform(획일적인)은 rather than single과 같은 의미라 ❼과 모순. 요약문 해석: 회의론자들은 세계 시민 정체성을 (A) 비현실적이라고 여길지 모르지만, 국가 정체성 자체도 인류 역사에서 비교적 (B) 최근의 발전이다. 우리의 책임은 가족, 공동체, 그리고 전 세계 사람들에게까지 미치므로, 우리가 누구인가에 대한 인식은 단일하기보다는 (C) 다면적이어야 한다.
choice.psg: ❶ We might not think of ourselves as global citizens yet, but it’s both necessary and possible to do so. ❷ Some people are skeptical about the idea of global citizenship, but for most of human history, people didn’t think of themselves as citizens of nation-states. ❸ After all, for most of human history, nation-states didn’t exist. ❹ The rise of nation-states over the last few centuries has led people to add state citizenship to other identities, such as family, people group, or religion. ❺ Given the connections between people around the world and the common challenges we face, we need to layer global citizenship on to these other identities. ❻ This doesn’t mean that global citizenship replaces these other identities. ❼ There’s not a single story about our identities. ❽ Instead, it’s precisely because we have obligations to our families, those in our community, and those around the world.
choice.body: Skeptics may find global citizenship (A)________, but national identity itself is a relatively (B)________ development in human history. Since our responsibilities reach our families, our communities, and people across the world, our sense of who we are should be (C)________ rather than single.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: Having a global identity does not require people to stop seeing themselves as members of a family.
Identities such as family and religion came before state citizenship in human history.
The writer believes national identity will gradually lose its importance as global ties grow stronger.
The writer expects that some readers may question the value of seeing themselves as global citizens.
Being a citizen of a nation-state is a relatively new way for people to define themselves.
choice.ex: ③ 필자는 ❺ 세계 시민 정체성을 기존 정체성 ‘위에’ 쌓자고 하며, ❻ 그것이 다른 정체성들을 대체하지 않는다고 분명히 말한다. 국가 정 체성이 점차 중요성을 잃는다는 예측은 본문에 없고 오히려 ❻의 취지와 어긋난다(세계적 연결이라는 본문 소재를 이용한 그럴듯한 함정). ① 근거 ❻ — 세계적 정체성을 갖는다고 해서 사람들이 자신을 가족의 일원으로 보는 것을 그만둘 필요는 없다. ② 근거 ❸❹ — 가족과 종교 같은 정체성은 인류 역사에서 국가 시민 정체성보다 먼저 생겨났다. ③ 근거 없음(정답) — 필자는 세계적 유대가 강해짐에 따라 국가 정체성이 점차 중요성을 잃을 것이라고 믿는다. ④ 근거 ❶❷ — 필자는 일부 독자들이 스스로를 세계 시민으로 보는 것의 가치에 의문을 제기할 수 있다고 예상한다. ⑤ 근거 ❷❸❹ — 국민 국가의 시민이라는 것은 사람들이 자신을 정의하는 비교적 새로운 방식이다.
choice.psg: ❶ We might not think of ourselves as global citizens yet, but it’s both necessary and possible to do so. ❷ Some people are skeptical about the idea of global citizenship, but for most of human history, people didn’t think of themselves as citizens of nation-states. ❸ After all, for most of human history, nation-states didn’t exist. ❹ The rise of nation-states over the last few centuries has led people to add state citizenship to other identities, such as family, people group, or religion. ❺ Given the connections between people around the world and the common challenges we face, we need to layer global citizenship on to these other identities. ❻ This doesn’t mean that global citizenship replaces these other identities. ❼ There’s not a single story about our identities. ❽ Instead, it’s precisely because we have obligations to our families, those in our community, and those around the world.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: people can hold several identities at once instead of having just one
every person’s life can be told as one complete and consistent story
our family stories matter far more than the history of our nation
no one has yet written a full history of how human identity developed
global citizenship should eventually take the place of national identity
choice.ex: ① 밑줄 해석: 우리의 정체성들에 관한 단 하나의 이야기가 있는 것은 아니다 → 한 사람이 여러 정체성을 동시에 지닐 수 있다 해설: 앞 문장 ❻은 세계 시민 정체성이 다른 정체성들을 ‘대체하지 않는다’고 했고, 뒤 문장 ❽은 우리가 가족·공동체·전 세계 사람들에 대해 동시에 의무를 진다 고 한다. 따라서 ‘정체성에 관한 단 하나의 이야기는 없다’는 것은 한 사람이 여러 겹의 정체성을 함께 지닌다는 뜻이다. ‘하나의 완결된 이야기’는 정반대, ‘아직 아무도 역사를 쓰지 않았다’는 story를 문자 그대로 읽은 함정, ‘세계 시민 정체성이 국가 정체성을 대신해야 한다’는 ❻과 모순, ‘가족 이야기가 더 중요하다’는 본문에 없는 가치 판단. ① 사람들은 하나만 갖는 대신 여러 정체성을 동시에 지닐 수 있다 ② 모든 사람의 삶은 하나의 완결되고 일관된 이야기로 전해질 수 있다 ③ 우리 가족의 이야기가 우리 국가의 역사보다 훨씬 더 중요하다 ④ 인간 정체성이 어떻게 발전했는지에 대한 완전한 역사를 아직 아무도 쓰지 않았다 ⑤ 세계 시민 정체성이 결국 국가 정체성을 대신해야 한다
choice.body: This doesn’t mean that global citizenship replaces these other identities. There’s not a single story about our identities. Instead, it’s precisely because we have obligations to our families, those in our community, and those around the world.
choice.ul: There’s not a single story about our identities.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) passively await — (B) superficial — (C) dissatisfied
(A) actively resist — (B) fundamental — (C) fulfilled
(A) actively resist — (B) superficial — (C) dissatisfied
(A) passively await — (B) superficial — (C) fulfilled
(A) passively await — (B) fundamental — (C) dissatisfied
choice.ex: ① (A) passively await (B) superficial (C) dissatisfied 근거 ❶❷❹❺❼ 해설: (A) ❶ 언젠가 기적적으로 바뀌리라는 믿음 + ❷ 하는 일이 거의 없음 = 수동적으로 기다리다(passively await) / (B) ❹ 비슷한 직책 검색, ❺ 무언가 하 는 것처럼 ‘느끼게’ 할 뿐 = 피상적인(superficial) / (C) ❺ just as disenchanted as they were before = 불만족스러운(dissatisfied). actively resist(적 극적으로 저항하다)는 ❶의 기대와 반대, fundamental(근본적인)은 ❻ 타이타닉의 갑판 의자 비유·❼ 접근 방식을 완전히 바꾸라는 결론과 모순, fulfilled(성 취감을 느끼는)는 ❺와 반대. 요약문 해석: 불행한 직업인들은 흔히 실질적인 변화를 만드는 대신 갑작스러운 운의 반전을 (A) 수동적으로 기다린다. 비슷한 자리로 옮기는 것은 생산적으로 느껴질 수 있지만, 그것은 그들을 이전만큼 (C) 불만족스러운 상태로 남겨 두는 (B) 피상적인 노력이므로, 완전히 새로운 접근 방식이 필요하다.
choice.psg: ❶ Among unsatisfied professionals, there’s a repeating theme — the belief that someday (a mysterious day in the future) things will miraculously change and they’ll stumble into the perfect job or career. ❷ At the same time, they (typically) do little to meaningfully alter their current situation. ❸ They don’t like their job, so what do they do? ❹ They head to job boards and search for roles with a similar job title, hoping that the universe will sprinkle a bit of magic on their career if they just hit the refresh button in a different department or company. ❺ Efforts like this make professionals feel like they are doing something, when really they’re just setting themselves up to take a new role and quickly become just as disenchanted as they were before. ❻ It’s like rearranging deck chairs on the Titanic. ❼ You’ve got to completely switch up your approach. ❽ If you keep playing the same game, you’ll win the same prizes.
choice.body: Unhappy professionals often (A)________ a sudden turn of fortune instead of making real changes. Moving to a similar position may feel productive, but it is a(n) (B)________ effort that leaves them as (C)________ as before, so a completely new approach is needed.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) genuine — (B) at the core — (C) identical
(A) false — (B) on the surface — (C) identical
(A) genuine — (B) on the surface — (C) different
(A) false — (B) at the core — (C) different
(A) false — (B) at the core — (C) identical
choice.ex: ⑤ (A) false (B) at the core (C) identical 근거 ❹❺❻❽ 해설: (A) ❺ 무언가를 하고 있는 것처럼 느끼게 하지만(feel like) 실제로는(when really) 그렇지 않음 = 거짓된(false) / (B) ❻ 침몰하는 배의 의자 배치만 바 꾸는 것 = 근본적으로는(at the core) 아무것도 바뀌지 않음 / (C) ❽ 같은 게임을 하면 똑같은 보상 = 똑같은(identical). genuine(진정한)은 ❺의 when really 대조와 반대, on the surface(겉으로는)는 회사·부서를 옮기는 겉모습의 변화가 실제로 있으므로 ‘아무것도 바꾸지 않는다’와 맞지 않음, different(다 른)는 ❽과 반대. 요약문 해석: 같은 직함의 일자리를 찾는 것은 사람들에게 (A) 거짓된 진전의 느낌을 주지만, (B) 근본적으로는 아무것도 바꾸지 않는다. 같은 전략을 반복하는 한, 그들은 (C) 똑같은 결과를 예상해야 한다.
choice.psg: ❶ Among unsatisfied professionals, there’s a repeating theme — the belief that someday (a mysterious day in the future) things will miraculously change and they’ll stumble into the perfect job or career. ❷ At the same time, they (typically) do little to meaningfully alter their current situation. ❸ They don’t like their job, so what do they do? ❹ They head to job boards and search for roles with a similar job title, hoping that the universe will sprinkle a bit of magic on their career if they just hit the refresh button in a different department or company. ❺ Efforts like this make professionals feel like they are doing something, when really they’re just setting themselves up to take a new role and quickly become just as disenchanted as they were before. ❻ It’s like rearranging deck chairs on the Titanic. ❼ You’ve got to completely switch up your approach. ❽ If you keep playing the same game, you’ll win the same prizes.
choice.body: Searching for roles with the same title gives people a(n) (A)________ sense of progress, yet it changes nothing (B)________. As long as they repeat the same strategy, they should expect (C)________ results.

choice.ex: ③ 필자는 비슷한 직무로 옮기는 것을 비판하지만(❹❺❻), 그 대안으로 ‘현재 직장에 머물라’고 하지 않는다. 필자의 처방은 ❼ ‘접근 방식 을 완전히 바꾸라’는 것이며, 오히려 ❷ 현재 상황을 바꾸려 하지 않는 태도 자체를 문제로 본다(이직 비판을 ‘머물라’로 확대 해석한 함정). ① 근거 ❼❽ — 다른 결과를 얻으려면 자신의 경력에 접근하는 전반적인 방식을 바꿔야 한다. ② 근거 ❹❺ — 다른 회사의 비슷한 직무로 옮기는 것은 진전이 있다는 인상을 줄 수 있다. ③ 근거 없음(정답) — 필자는 불행한 직업인들에게 만족을 느낄 때까지 현재 직장에 머물라고 조언한다. ④ 근거 ❷ — 자기 일을 싫어하는 직업인들은 흔히 현재 상황을 개선하기 위한 실질적인 행동을 피한다. ⑤ 근거 ❺❻ — 필자는 사소한 경력상의 이동을 침몰하는 배 위에서의 무의미한 행동에 비유한다.
choice.psg: ❶ Among unsatisfied professionals, there’s a repeating theme — the belief that someday (a mysterious day in the future) things will miraculously change and they’ll stumble into the perfect job or career. ❷ At the same time, they (typically) do little to meaningfully alter their current situation. ❸ They don’t like their job, so what do they do? ❹ They head to job boards and search for roles with a similar job title, hoping that the universe will sprinkle a bit of magic on their career if they just hit the refresh button in a different department or company. ❺ Efforts like this make professionals feel like they are doing something, when really they’re just setting themselves up to take a new role and quickly become just as disenchanted as they were before. ❻ It’s like rearranging deck chairs on the Titanic. ❼ You’ve got to completely switch up your approach. ❽ If you keep playing the same game, you’ll win the same prizes.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

choice.ex: ④ 밑줄 해석: 이는 타이타닉호의 갑판 의자들을 재배치하는 것과 같다 → 근본 문제는 그대로 둔 채 겉모습만 바꾸는 쓸모없는 노력 해설: 침몰하는 타이타닉호에서 갑판 의자의 위치를 바꾸는 것은 배가 가라앉는다는 근본 문제에 아무 도움이 되지 않는 행동이다. 앞 문장 ❺(무언가 하는 것처 럼 느끼지만 금세 다시 환상이 깨짐)와 뒤 문장 ❼(접근 방식을 완전히 바꿔야 함)이 ‘겉모습만 바꾸는 쓸모없는 노력’이라는 의미를 확인해 준다. ‘신중하게 정리 해 순조롭게’는 비유를 긍정적으로 읽은 정반대, ‘회사가 문제에 부딪히기 직전에 그만두기’는 침몰하는 배를 문자 그대로 읽은 함정, ‘너무 많은 업무’는 무관, ‘대 부분의 경력이 비참하게 끝난다’는 과도한 일반화. ① 직장에서 너무 많은 업무를 떠맡아 결국 압도당하는 느낌을 받는 것 ② 회사가 심각한 문제에 부딪히기 직전에 직장을 그만두는 것 ③ 경력이 더 순조롭게 진행되도록 자신의 일을 신중하게 정리하는 것 ④ 경력의 근본적인 문제를 해결하지 못하는 쓸모없는 변화를 만드는 것 ⑤ 대부분의 경력은 결국 비참한 결말을 맞을 것임을 받아들이는 것
